neighbours.label: gardening text about grass, lawns and plant stems (mowing, turf, stalks, canes, clippings), as against the same cutting and height wording about hair, buildings or other things
fire: Set the mower blades high so that the grass shades its own roots in July.
Leave the clippings on the lawn after mowing to return nitrogen to the soil.
Prune the old canes of the raspberry bushes down to the ground after fruiting.
Kentucky bluegrass spreads by rhizomes and fills bare patches in the turf.
Cut back the dead stalks of the perennials before new shoots appear.
Overseed thin areas of the yard with ryegrass in early autumn.
Water the lawn deeply once a week rather than lightly every evening.
Strip the thyme leaves from the woody stems before chopping them.
quiet: Set the oven rack high so that the bread browns on top in the last minutes.
Leave the clippings on the floor after the haircut and sweep them up later.
Prune the old files in the archive down to the last five years after the audit.
Kentucky's new airport spreads across two terminals and fills a former farm.
Cut back the long hours of the night shift before the new staff arrive.
Repaint thin areas of the fence with white primer in early autumn.
Wash the car thoroughly once a week rather than quickly every evening.
Strip the old paint from the wooden door before sanding it.
